title: Failure didn’t disqualify them.
paragraphs:
Failure didn’t disqualify them.
It deployed them.

Peter denied.
Thomas doubted.
Most of them disappeared when the cross got heavy.
And the first word Jesus gives them after the resurrection?

Not “Explain yourself.”
Not “Do better.”
Not “Earn it back.”

Matthew 28 doesn’t start with pressure. It starts with power.
“All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to Me.”

You don’t go in your consistency.
You go in His authority.
You don’t go because you’re impressive.
You go because He is risen.

Grace is not a retirement plan for your past.
It’s a deployment strategy.

Jesus could have chosen angels.
He chose redeemed failures.

That means your worst chapter is not your ending.
It’s your commissioning ceremony.

Maybe your “GO” isn’t overseas.
Maybe it’s across the table.
Across the office.
Across the group chat.

The tomb is empty.
The mission is not.
If you feel unqualified, you’re exactly the kind of person He sends.

Grace and peace, mga kapatid.
Obedience over optics.
